articles.what: Warm sunset angular sweep fading from orange through magenta and violet into deep navy Up close: Soft cloudy blotches of orange, red-pink, magenta and violet, 80 to 200 px across, covered in a dense field of small cream-white vertical dashes about 3 px wide and 8 to 12 px tall, like rain or stitching. A faint paper-like grain sits under the dashes. From a distance: Reads as an orange, pink and purple sunset fade with a white speckle all over, like confetti or rain on a poster; the dashes dominate close up and fade to a bright sparkle at distance. Measured spec (average): metal 221, roughness 80, coat 221. Shine: satin. Metal: full. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: gt / sports car, stock car, show car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Prizm Sunset Strip" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and sides: wide panels show the cloud colours
Body base with navy or white trim
White dashes cut into numbers; use thick navy or black numbers with a white outline, white numbers vanish.
Plain stripes or number plates in navy or white: only simple shapes survive
Pairs well with: navy, black, white, chrome.
pitfalls: Not an angular sunset sweep: the colour zones are soft rounded clouds, not hard angled bands
Not navy dominant: deep blue only appears as small violet pools
Avoid: busy stripes hide door numbers, keep graphics off the sweep.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 221 (true metallic), roughness 80 (satin gloss), clearcoat 221 (almost no clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: busy stripes hide door numbers, keep graphics off the sweep.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: plain stripes or number plates in navy or white: only simple shapes survive; thin dark pinstripes: sharpen against the bright field
Patterns to avoid: dots, rain or glitter patterns: duplicate the dashes; fine grain or camo: clutter
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat strip: calms a panel; avoid sparkle spec: it already glitters
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

Thin pale hairline scratches curve across at random. From a distance: Reads as a blotchy rainbow-anodised metal, blue and purple with warm gold-rose patches; no pattern, just big colour clouds. A darker green haze moves faintly under it. From a distance: Reads as a dark green-black with a lime glitter, like a toxic fizz; the rings merge into a speckled neon green sparkle. From a distance: Reads as dark green-black with a fine yellow-lime glitter and a faint wavy vertical streak; moody and toxic but quiet. Measured spec (average): metal 227, roughness 55, coat 234.
